syntax_error:
-- Look just before "{token}": a missing comma, an unclosed ' or ( , or a keyword from another database.
-- MySQL uses `backticks` for names and 'single quotes' for text; LIMIT offset, count is fine here.
unknown_table:
-- If it should exist: run the missing migration, or check you're connected to the right database:
SELECT DATABASE();
unknown_column: -- then use the real column name in the query
ambiguous_column:
-- Put the table (or its alias) in front of the column everywhere it appears:
SELECT t1.{column}, ... FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON ... WHERE t1.{column} = ...;
unknown_function: -- MySQL equivalents: STRING_AGG -> GROUP_CONCAT, COALESCE works, NOW() works, ILIKE -> LIKE (case-insensitive by default collation)
duplicate_key:
-- See the row that already has this value:
SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE <unique column> = '{value}';
fk_missing_parent:
-- Check the parent exists:
SELECT * FROM {parent} WHERE {parent_column} = <the value you saved in {column}>;
-- Create the parent first, or save the child with an existing {parent}.{parent_column}.
fk_has_children:
-- See how many rows still point to it:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {child} WHERE {column} = <the id you're deleting>;
not_null:
-- Send a value for {column}, or give the column a default:
ALTER TABLE {table} MODIFY {column} <its type> NOT NULL DEFAULT <value>;
value_too_long:
SELECT MAX(CHAR_LENGTH({column})) FROM {table};
SHOW COLUMNS FROM {table} LIKE '{column}';
ALTER TABLE {table} MODIFY {column} VARCHAR(255);  -- or TEXT for long text
out_of_range: ALTER TABLE {table} MODIFY {column} BIGINT;  -- or DECIMAL(15,2) for money
bad_value_type:
-- Send a real {column} value: numbers without commas, dates as 'YYYY-MM-DD', NULL (not '') when empty.
-- To read a date like '{value}': STR_TO_DATE('{value}', '%d-%m-%Y')
check_violation: SELECT CHECK_CLAUSE FROM information_schema.CHECK_CONSTRAINTS WHERE CONSTRAINT_NAME = '{constraint}';
-- then save a value that meets that rule
charset_mismatch:
ALTER DATABASE <db> CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
ALTER TABLE {table} CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
-- and in the app's connection: charset=utf8mb4
disk_full:
-- Common mistake: deleting binary log files with rm. The server's .index list still names them (MySQL then refuses PURGE BINARY LOGS
-- until the .index file is fixed) and a replica that still needed them breaks. Always remove them with PURGE BINARY LOGS.
out_of_memory:
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'innodb_buffer_pool_size';
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'max_connections';

-- In my.cnf, size it to the server (database-only: ~60% of RAM; shared server: much less), then restart:
innodb_buffer_pool_size = <e.g. 1G on a 4 GB shared server>
max_connections = <what the app really needs>
packet_too_large:
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'max_allowed_packet';
SET GLOBAL max_allowed_packet = 64*1024*1024;  -- also set it in my.cnf to keep it after restart
-- Better: insert in batches and keep files outside the database.
temp_space_full:
-- Add an index for the GROUP BY / ORDER BY columns of that query, then:
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'tmp_table_size'; SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'max_heap_table_size';
statement_timeout: EXPLAIN <your query>;  -- look for type = ALL and a big rows number
-- Add the index EXPLAIN is missing; paste the query here and I'll write it.
full_scan:
-- Paste the query and I'll give the exact index, e.g.:
ALTER TABLE {table} ADD INDEX idx_{table}_{column} ({column});
deadlock: SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS;  -- the LATEST DETECTED DEADLOCK section shows both transactions and the rows
-- In code: update rows in the same order (e.g. ORDER BY id) and retry the transaction when error 1213 comes back.
lock_wait:
-- Who is blocking whom:
SELECT r.trx_id waiting, r.trx_query waiting_query, b.trx_id blocking, b.trx_query blocking_query, b.trx_started
FROM information_schema.innodb_trx b JOIN performance_schema.data_lock_waits w ON w.BLOCKING_ENGINE_TRANSACTION_ID = b.trx_id
JOIN information_schema.innodb_trx r ON r.trx_id = w.REQUESTING_ENGINE_TRANSACTION_ID;
-- If a forgotten transaction blocks: KILL <its thread id>;  (after checking what it is)
serialization_failure: -- Retry the whole transaction 2-3 times with a short wait when it fails.
idle_transaction: SELECT trx_id, trx_started, trx_mysql_thread_id FROM information_schema.innodb_trx ORDER BY trx_started LIMIT 5;
-- then KILL <trx_mysql_thread_id>; and fix the code path that leaves it open
metadata_lock:
SELECT * FROM performance_schema.metadata_locks WHERE OBJECT_NAME = '{table}';
SHOW PROCESSLIST;

-- End the long transaction holding the table, then run the ALTER off-peak with:
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 5;
access_denied:
-- As an admin, check how the user exists:
SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE user = '{user}';

-- Reset the password for the host the app connects from:
ALTER USER '{user}'@'{host_pattern}' IDENTIFIED BY '<new password>';
host_not_allowed:
CREATE USER '{user}'@'{host}' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>';
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON <db>.* TO '{user}'@'{host}';
-- On cPanel hosting: Remote MySQL -> add {host}
server_unreachable:
-- On the database server:
systemctl status mysql   # is it running?
ss -ltnp | grep 3306     # is it listening, on which address?
-- For remote access, bind-address in my.cnf must not be 127.0.0.1, and the firewall must allow 3306 from the app server.
connection_lost: -- In the app: reconnect/ping before reusing an idle connection.
permission_denied: GRANT {token} ON <db>.{table} TO '{user}'@'{host}';  -- only the right that's missing
ssl_required: -- Connect with SSL, e.g. mysql --ssl-mode=REQUIRED ..., or in PHP PDO: PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_SSL_CA => '/path/ca.pem'
replica_lag:
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G   -- MySQL 8.0.22+; older MySQL and MariaDB: SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G
-- Seconds_Behind_Source = how far behind; Relay_Log_Space growing = changes arrive faster than they are applied

-- Find which of these it is, then fix that one:
-- 1) one huge UPDATE/DELETE on the primary: redo such jobs in small batches (e.g. 5,000 rows per transaction)
-- 2) tables without a PRIMARY KEY under row-based logging: every row change searches the whole table on the replica, so add a primary key
-- 3) one apply thread: use parallel apply (replica_parallel_workers; MariaDB: slave_parallel_threads)
-- 4) a weaker or busy replica (slow disk, long reports running there)
-- Reads that must see a save made a moment ago (login, checkout) should go to the primary, not the replica.
replication_stopped:
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G   -- MariaDB/older: SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G
-- Last_SQL_Errno / Last_SQL_Error (or Last_IO_Error) is the real reason; MySQL 8 also: SELECT * FROM performance_schema.replication_applier_status_by_worker\G

-- Common mistake: SET GLOBAL sql_replica_skip_counter = 1 (sql_slave_skip_counter) or slave_skip_errors as the fix.
-- Each skip throws a change away, the replica silently drifts further, and the next error comes back worse.
-- If many rows differ, rebuild the replica from a fresh backup of the primary instead.

-- Stop new drift: make the replica refuse app writes:
SET GLOBAL super_read_only = ON;   -- MySQL (MariaDB: SET GLOBAL read_only = ON;)
source_log_purged:
-- The changes the replica needs no longer exist on the primary, so it can't be repaired by restarting.
-- Safe fix: rebuild the replica from a fresh, consistent backup of the primary
-- (mysqldump --single-transaction --source-data=2, MariaDB: mariadb-dump --single-transaction --master-data=2, or a physical backup), then start replication from the position recorded in it.

-- Common mistake: pointing the replica at the next log file that still exists (CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_LOG_FILE=...).
-- It starts again, but every change in the deleted files is silently missing on the replica.

-- Before purging logs in future, check what each replica has read:
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G   -- on each replica: Source_Log_File (MariaDB: Master_Log_File)
SHOW BINARY LOGS;        -- on the primary
-- and keep logs longer than a replica could be down: binlog_expire_logs_seconds
write_on_replica: SELECT @@hostname, @@port, @@read_only, @@super_read_only;   -- read_only = 1: this server is a replica or switched to read-only

-- Send writes to the primary: check the host in the app's database config (or the writer endpoint of your cloud database).
-- After a failover, restart or recycle the app's connection pool so it stops using connections to the old primary.
-- Common mistake: SET GLOBAL read_only = OFF on a replica to make the error go away; writes there make it drift and stop replication later.
binlog_not_expiring:
SELECT @@log_bin, @@binlog_expire_logs_seconds;
SHOW BINARY LOGS;   -- how many files and how big (needs REPLICATION CLIENT / BINLOG MONITOR)

-- First check what every replica still needs: SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G on each (Source_Log_File; MariaDB: Master_Log_File).
-- Then remove only older files, and set an expiry that outlasts the slowest replica (here 7 days):
PURGE BINARY LOGS BEFORE NOW() - INTERVAL 7 DAY;
SET GLOBAL binlog_expire_logs_seconds = 604800;   -- and the same in my.cnf, or it resets on restart

-- Common mistake: rm on binary log files, or turning log_bin off to save space.
-- rm leaves the .index list and replicas out of step; log_bin off breaks replication and point-in-time restore.

unknown_table.sql: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()

unknown_column.sql: SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name = :table

resolve.sql: SELECT table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.statistics WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND index_name = :key ORDER BY seq_in_index LIMIT 1
SELECT referenced_table_name, referenced_column_name FROM information_schema.key_column_usage WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND constraint_name = :constraint LIMIT 1

value_too_long.sql: SELECT character_maximum_length FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name = :table AND column_name = :column

sql: SELECT variable_value FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE variable_name = 'Max_used_connections'

lock_wait.sql: SELECT trx_id, trx_started, trx_query FROM information_schema.innodb_trx WHERE trx_started < NOW() - INTERVAL 30 SECOND

idle_transaction.sql: SELECT trx_id, trx_started, trx_mysql_thread_id FROM information_schema.innodb_trx WHERE trx_query IS NULL AND trx_started < NOW() - INTERVAL 60 SECOND

write_on_replica.proof: this server has read_only = ON (it only accepts reads)

binlog_not_expiring.sql: SELECT 1 FROM performance_schema.global_variables v WHERE UPPER(v.variable_name) = 'LOG_BIN' AND v.variable_value = 'ON' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM performance_schema.global_variables e WHERE UPPER(e.variable_name) IN ('BINLOG_EXPIRE_LOGS_SECONDS', 'EXPIRE_LOGS_DAYS') AND e.variable_value + 0 > 0)
binlog_not_expiring.proof: binary logging is on and no expiry is set, so old binary logs are never removed

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS type), which works on every database.
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS type) likho, ye har database pe chalta hai.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS SIGNED) (MySQL/MariaDB's integer cast).
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS SIGNED) likho (MySQL/MariaDB ka integer cast).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
{db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS type) with {db}'s type names (CHAR, SIGNED, DECIMAL(p,s), DATE, DATETIME).
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS type) likho, {db} ke type naamon ke saath (CHAR, SIGNED, DECIMAL(p,s), DATE, DATETIME).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein ILIKE nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use LIKE: with the usual case-insensitive (_ci) collation it already ignores case. On a _bin or _cs column, compare LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER('...').
refuses.fix_hi: LIKE likho: aam _ci collation pe ye pehle se case ignore karta hai. _bin/_cs column pe LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER('...').

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein DISTINCT ON nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: For one row per group, number the rows with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) in a subquery and keep rn = 1 (MySQL 8 / MariaDB 10.2+).
refuses.fix_hi: Har group ki ek row ke liye subquery mein ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) lagao aur rn = 1 rakho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein NULLS LAST nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Sort on 'x IS NULL' first (false before true), then on x.
refuses.fix_hi: Pehle 'x IS NULL' pe sort karo (false pehle), phir x pe.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein NULLS FIRST nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Sort on 'x IS NOT NULL' first (NULL rows first), then on x.
refuses.fix_hi: Pehle 'x IS NOT NULL' pe sort karo (NULL rows pehle), phir x pe.

refuses.error: error 1305, FUNCTION GETDATE does not exist
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein GETDATE() nahi hota (wo SQL Server ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use NOW() (date and time) or CURDATE() (date only).
refuses.fix_hi: NOW() (date aur time) ya CURDATE() (sirf date) likho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein $1 placeholder nahi hote (wo PostgreSQL ke hain)
refuses.fix_en: MySQL/MariaDB drivers use ? (or named :name placeholders in PDO).
refuses.fix_hi: MySQL/MariaDB drivers ? (ya PDO mein :name) use karte hain.

refuses.title_en: {db} doesn't quote names with [brackets] (that's SQL Server)
refuses.title_hi: {db} naam [brackets] mein nahi maanta (wo SQL Server ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Quote a name with `backticks` (or leave a plain name bare).
refuses.fix_hi: Naam `backticks` mein likho (ya saadharan naam bina quote ke).

refuses.title_en: {db} reads SYSDATE without () as a column (that's Oracle)
refuses.title_hi: {db} bina () ke SYSDATE ko column samajhta hai (wo Oracle ka hai)

refuses.title_en: {db} has no SYSDATETIME() / GETUTCDATE() (that's SQL Server)

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein !~ nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use NOT REGEXP (it ignores case with the usual _ci collation).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein ~ regex nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use REGEXP (it ignores case with the usual _ci collation, like PostgreSQL's ~*).
Use LIKE for % and _ patterns, or REGEXP for a regular expression (rewrite the pattern: SIMILAR TO's | and () mean the regex ones, but it must match the whole text, so add ^ and $).
refuses.fix_hi: LIKE ya REGEXP likho (pattern ke aage ^ aur peeche $).

refuses.fix_en: Run the UPDATE, then SELECT the same rows (same WHERE) inside the same transaction. (MariaDB 10.5+ has RETURNING for INSERT and DELETE only; MySQL has none.)
refuses.fix_hi: UPDATE ke baad usi transaction mein wahi rows SELECT karo.

refuses.error: error 1305, FUNCTION generate_series does not exist (1064 in FROM)
refuses.fix_en: Make the numbers with a recursive WITH: WITH RECURSIVE s(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM s WHERE n < 10) SELECT n FROM s (MariaDB also has seq_1_to_10 tables with its Sequence engine).

limit_in_subquery.says: MySQL and MariaDB refuse LIMIT inside IN / ANY / ALL / SOME (error 1235, doesn't yet support 'LIMIT & IN/ALL/ANY/SOME subquery').

derived_alias.says: MySQL refuses a subquery in FROM without a name (error 1248, Every derived table must have its own alias); MariaDB stops with a syntax error (1064).

sum_boolean.says: MySQL and MariaDB treat true as 1 and false as 0, so SUM(condition) counts the matches there.

having_alias.says: MySQL and MariaDB let HAVING use a name made in SELECT.

count_distinct_multi.says: MySQL and MariaDB accept COUNT(DISTINCT a, b) and skip a combination that has a NULL in it.

window_over_ungrouped.says: MariaDB runs it and takes the plain column from one row of each group (silently wrong); MySQL refuses it when ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY is on (its default).

update_join.says: MySQL and MariaDB write a joined UPDATE as UPDATE a JOIN b ON ... SET a.col = ... (or UPDATE a, b SET ... WHERE ...).

update_from.says: MySQL and MariaDB have no FROM in UPDATE: UPDATE a SET ... FROM b stops with error 1064 (syntax error near 'FROM').

set_qualified.says: MySQL and MariaDB accept SET alias.col = ... (in a joined UPDATE they need it).

delete_join.says: MySQL and MariaDB delete through a join as DELETE a FROM a JOIN b ON ... WHERE ...

delete_using.says: MySQL and MariaDB read DELETE FROM a USING b differently (the USING list must contain a): it stops with error 1064 when a has an alias, or 1109 (Unknown table in MULTI DELETE).

on_duplicate_key.says: MySQL and MariaDB upsert with INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col = VALUES(col).

on_conflict.says: MySQL and MariaDB don't know ON CONFLICT: error 1064 (syntax error near 'CONFLICT').

change_limit.says: MySQL and MariaDB accept ORDER BY and LIMIT on a single-table UPDATE or DELETE.

insert_ignore.says: MySQL and MariaDB accept INSERT IGNORE.

replace_into.says: MySQL and MariaDB accept REPLACE INTO.

case_mixed_types.says: MySQL and MariaDB run it but turn the whole CASE column into text, so the numbers then sort and compare as text ('1000' before '50').

recursion_limit.says: MySQL 8 stops after cte_max_recursion_depth (1000) rounds with error 3636 (Recursive query aborted after 1001 iterations); MariaDB stops after max_recursive_iterations (1000) rounds with NO error and returns only the rows made so far.

recursive_text_width.says: MySQL and MariaDB size a text column from the anchor ('x' is one character, a VARCHAR(40) column is 40), and a longer value from the recursive part stops the query with error 1406 (Data too long for column) in strict mode.

window_needs_order.says: MariaDB refuses LAG, LEAD, RANK, DENSE_RANK, PERCENT_RANK and CUME_DIST without ORDER BY in the window (error 4018, No order list in window specification); MySQL 8 runs them in an arbitrary order.

like_prefix_index.says: On MySQL/MariaDB an ordinary index serves LIKE 'abc%' as a range (lab: type range on MariaDB 10.11).

text_vs_number.says: MySQL/MariaDB turn every value of the column into a number to compare it, so the index can't be used (lab: type index / ALL) and '098...' and '98... ' match too (a 1292 note, no error).

or_same_table.says: MariaDB combines two indexes for an OR on one table (EXPLAIN: index_merge, Using union(a,b)).

expression_index.says: MySQL 8.0.13+ can index an expression (INDEX ((LOWER(email)))). MariaDB 10.11 can't: add a virtual column (email_lc VARCHAR(80) AS (LOWER(email)) VIRTUAL, INDEX (email_lc)) and compare that column by name; the lab showed WHERE LOWER(email) = ... still reads the whole index.

offset_reads.says: MariaDB's EXPLAIN for ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 OFFSET 15000 shows rows = 15020: every skipped row is read.

optimizer_sargable.says: MariaDB 11.1+ turns DATE(col) and YEAR(col) compared with a constant into a range on the index by itself (the CI run on MariaDB 11 also did it for LEFT(col, n) = 'abc'); MariaDB 10.11 and MySQL 8 don't (lab: 10.11 read the whole index). The bare-column form is fast on every version and on PostgreSQL.

skip_locked.says: MySQL 8.0.1+ and MariaDB 10.6+ have SKIP LOCKED (lab: MariaDB 10.11 gave the second worker job 2 at once); NOWAIT on MariaDB fails at once with 1205 (MySQL 8: 3572).

lock_scan.says: MySQL/MariaDB (InnoDB) lock every index record the search reads: with no index on the WHERE's column that is every row, so a second session changing another row waits (lab: 1205 after the lock wait timeout).

gap_locks.says: Under REPEATABLE READ (the InnoDB default) a range change also locks the gaps: an INSERT into the range waits (lab: 1205).

deadlock.says: MySQL/MariaDB stop one of the two with 1213 (SQLSTATE 40001, Deadlock found when trying to get lock) and roll it back; SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS keeps the LATEST DETECTED DEADLOCK.

schema_rules.about: How MySQL/MariaDB take a CREATE TABLE (night 6): what they refuse, what they silently change, and their limits. Lab: MariaDB 10.11.

fk_auto_index.says: InnoDB makes an index on a foreign key column by itself when none leads with it.

utf8.says: 'utf8' is utf8mb3 (3 bytes): a 4-byte character (emoji) is refused in strict mode (1366 Incorrect string value).

myisam_fk.says: ENGINE=MyISAM accepts FOREIGN KEY / REFERENCES with no warning and never checks them.

inline_references.says: MariaDB 10.5+ keeps a column's inline REFERENCES as a real foreign key (lab: MariaDB 10.11 refused a missing parent, 1452). MySQL before 9.0 parsed it and ignored it (documented; not lab-tested here): write FOREIGN KEY (col) REFERENCES t (id) as its own line.

fk_same_type.says: Both ends of a foreign key need the same integer size and signedness; INT -> BIGINT, INT -> INT UNSIGNED and INT -> VARCHAR are refused (errno 150).

fk_target.says: A foreign key may point at any indexed parent column (a non-unique one is accepted, against the SQL standard); a parent column with no index is refused (errno 150).

max_row_bytes.says: All VARCHARs of a row together may use at most 65,535 bytes (characters x 4 in utf8mb4); one VARCHAR over 16,383 utf8mb4 characters is 1074.

text_primary_key.says: A TEXT / BLOB column can't be a primary key without a prefix length (1170). MariaDB 10.4+ accepts TEXT in UNIQUE (a hidden hash); MySQL refuses it there too (documented).

timestamp_range.says: TIMESTAMP holds 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-19 UTC (2106 on MariaDB 11.5+; 1292 outside it); DATETIME holds years 1000-9999.

varchar_needs_length.says: VARCHAR without a length is a syntax error.

schema_rules.reserved_note: Lab-tested on MariaDB 10.11 as bare table and column names. MySQL 8 also reserves rank, groups, window, lateral, row_number, lead, lag (documented, not lab-tested here).

explain.about: MySQL and MariaDB EXPLAIN: one row per table, in join order. type says how that table's rows are found; rows is the estimate (MariaDB ANALYZE adds r_rows, the real count, and r_filtered).

SYSTEM.hi: table mein ek hi row hai

CONST.en: at most one row, found by the primary key or a unique key compared with a value, read once
CONST.hi: primary/unique key se zyada se zyada ek row, ek hi baar

EQ_REF.en: one row for each row before it, by its primary or unique key (the best join step)
EQ_REF.hi: pichli har row ke liye primary/unique key se ek row (sabse achha join)

REF.en: the rows with one value of an index (a non-unique index, or a key prefix)
REF.hi: index ki ek value wali rows

REF_OR_NULL.en: like ref, plus the rows where the column IS NULL
REF_OR_NULL.hi: ref jaisa, saath mein NULL wali rows

RANGE.en: a stretch of an index (>, <, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE 'abc%')
RANGE.hi: index ka ek hissa (>, <, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE 'abc%')

INDEX_MERGE.en: two or more indexes read and their rows combined (an OR or AND across indexed columns)
INDEX_MERGE.hi: do ya zyada index padh ke rows milaayi

INDEX.en: the whole index is read, entry by entry (cheaper than the table, but every entry)
INDEX.hi: poora index entry-entry padha jaata hai

ALL.en: every row of the table is read and checked (a full table scan)
ALL.hi: table ki har row padh ke check hoti hai (full table scan)

UNIQUE_SUBQUERY.en: an IN subquery answered by a unique index lookup

INDEX_SUBQUERY.en: an IN subquery answered by an index lookup

Using index condition.en: part of the WHERE is checked inside the index before reading the row
Using index condition.hi: WHERE ka hissa row padhne se pehle index mein check

Using index for group-by.en: groups read straight from the index

Using index.en: everything needed is in the index (covering): the table itself isn't read
Using index.hi: saara data index mein hai (covering): table nahi padhi

Using where.en: rows are checked against the WHERE after they are read
Using where.hi: rows padhne ke baad WHERE se check

Using filesort.en: rows are sorted after they are found, not read in index order
Using filesort.hi: rows milne ke baad sort hoti hain

Using temporary.en: a temporary table holds the groups or distinct rows

Using join buffer.en: this table has no usable index for the join, so rows are matched in batches
Using join buffer.hi: join ke liye index nahi, rows batch mein milaayi jaati hain

Using union.en: rows from two indexes are combined (index merge for an OR)
Using union.hi: do index ki rows milaayi (OR ke liye)

Impossible WHERE.en: the WHERE can never be true: no row is read
Impossible WHERE.hi: WHERE kabhi true nahi: koi row nahi padhi

Range checked for each record.en: no good index is known in advance; one is chosen again for every row before it
Range checked for each record.hi: pichli har row ke liye index naye sire se chuna jaata hai

Table scan on.en: every row of the table is read
Table scan on.hi: table ki har row padhi jaati hai

Index scan on.en: the whole index is read in order
Index scan on.hi: poora index kram se padha jaata hai

Covering index scan on.en: the whole index is read; the table itself isn't needed

Index lookup on.en: rows with one value of an index
Index lookup on.hi: index ki ek value wali rows

Single-row index lookup on.en: one row by a unique key

Covering index lookup on.en: rows with one value, read from the index alone
Covering index lookup on.hi: ek value ki rows, sirf index se

Filter:.en: rows checked against a condition after they are read
Filter:.hi: padhne ke baad condition se check

Nested loop.en: for each row of the first input, the matching rows of the second are looked up
Nested loop.hi: pehle input ki har row ke liye doosre ki matching rows

Inner hash join.en: one side is put in a hash table and the other side probes it
Inner hash join.hi: ek taraf hash table, doosri usme dhoondhti hai

Sort:.en: rows sorted after they are found

Limit:.en: only the first rows are passed on

port.about: What MySQL/MariaDB refuse from other databases' SQL and how to say it in their words; and their interval, date-format and cast words. Every entry was run on MariaDB 10.11 (lab: tests/practice/test_night10.py).
port.cast_error: error 1064, syntax error near the type name
port.cast_manual_en: MySQL/MariaDB cast to CHAR, SIGNED, UNSIGNED, DECIMAL(p,s), DOUBLE, DATE, DATETIME or TIME; for a true/false value compare instead (x <> 0).

string_agg.error: error 1305, FUNCTION STRING_AGG does not exist
string_agg.fix_en: GROUP_CONCAT joins a group's values (ORDER BY and SEPARATOR inside it).
string_agg.fix_hi: GROUP_CONCAT group ki values jodta hai (ORDER BY aur SEPARATOR andar).

convert.error: error 1064, syntax error (MySQL's CONVERT takes the value first)
convert.fix_en: CAST(value AS type) says it in MySQL/MariaDB words (their CONVERT is CONVERT(value, type)).
convert.manual_en: Write CAST(value AS type) with a MySQL/MariaDB type (CHAR, SIGNED, DECIMAL(p,s), DATE, DATETIME).

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION DATEADD does not exist
calls.fix_en: DATE_ADD(date, INTERVAL n UNIT) adds to a date.

calls.error: error 1582, Incorrect parameter count in the call to native function 'DATEDIFF'
calls.fix_en: MySQL/MariaDB's DATEDIFF(end, start) takes two dates and gives days; other units come from TIMESTAMPDIFF(unit, start, end), which counts whole units (SQL Server counts the boundaries crossed: from 31 Dec to 1 Jan is 1 year there, 0 here).
calls.fix_hi: DATEDIFF(end, start) din deta hai; baaki units TIMESTAMPDIFF(unit, start, end).

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION DATEPART does not exist
calls.fix_en: EXTRACT(part FROM date) works on MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL alike.
calls.fix_hi: EXTRACT(part FROM date) har jagah chalta hai.

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION LEN does not exist
calls.fix_en: CHAR_LENGTH counts characters (LEN also ignores trailing spaces; wrap in TRIM if that matters).

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION CHARINDEX does not exist
calls.fix_en: LOCATE(text_to_find, text) takes the same arguments in the same order.

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION IIF does not exist
calls.fix_en: IF(condition, then, else) is the same on MySQL/MariaDB (CASE WHEN works everywhere).

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION STRPOS does not exist
calls.fix_en: LOCATE takes the text to find FIRST: STRPOS(text, x) = LOCATE(x, text) (POSITION(x IN text) works on both).
calls.fix_hi: LOCATE mein dhoondhne wala text pehle aata hai.

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION SPLIT_PART does not exist
calls.fix_en: SUBSTRING_INDEX(text, sep, 1) is the part before the first separator, like SPLIT_PART(text, sep, 1).
calls.manual_en: For the n-th part write SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(text, sep, n), sep, -1), and check rows with fewer parts (SPLIT_PART gives '' there).
calls.manual_hi: n-th hissa: SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(text, sep, n), sep, -1).

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION RANDOM does not exist
calls.fix_en: RAND() gives a random number from 0 to 1.

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION NEWID does not exist
error 1305, FUNCTION GEN_RANDOM_UUID does not exist
error 1305, FUNCTION DATE_TRUNC does not exist
calls.fix_en: The first day of the month / year is built from the date's own parts.
calls.fix_hi: Mahine/saal ka pehla din date ke hisson se banta hai.
calls.manual_en: For a week, hour or quarter, build the start from the date's parts (e.g. DATE_SUB(d, INTERVAL WEEKDAY(d) DAY) for the Monday).
calls.manual_hi: Week/hour ke liye date ke hisson se shuruaat banao.

calls.error: error 1305, FUNCTION TO_DATE does not exist
calls.fix_en: STR_TO_DATE reads text as a date with MySQL's % format codes.
calls.manual_en: Use STR_TO_DATE(text, '%d-%m-%Y') with MySQL's % codes (%Y year, %m month, %d day, %H hour, %i minute).

calls.fix_en: LAST_INSERT_ID() gives the id this connection inserted last.

join_number_text.says: MySQL compares a number with text as numbers: '01' and '1abc' match 1 (warning 1292), and no index on the text column is used.

add_not_null_no_default.says: Old rows get the type's implicit default ('' / 0) when a NOT NULL column is added without DEFAULT.

fk_makes_index.says: InnoDB creates an index for every FOREIGN KEY that has none.

verify.nullable: SELECT column_name, is_nullable, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = '{table}' AND column_name IN ({cols})
verify.nulls_now: SELECT COUNT(*) AS null_rows FROM {table} WHERE {col} IS NULL
verify.dupes: SELECT {cols}, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {table} GROUP BY {cols} HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 5
verify.plan_run_note: EXPLAIN ANALYZE (MySQL 8.0.18+) really runs a SELECT and shows the time and rows of each step; on a change statement use plain EXPLAIN.
verify.lab: information_schema, SHOW INDEX and EXPLAIN were run on MariaDB 10.11 (the MySQL family); EXPLAIN ANALYZE is MySQL 8.0.18+ syntax (MySQL manual), MariaDB refuses it with 1064.
